headline: High-risk default interaction: OpenHands can write/egress in a shared runtime, while the paired content-writing repo offers no isolation or trust boundaries.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile A is a content-writing repo with no runnable I/O surfaces, so it cannot directly ingest B's outputs. Profile B can read/write files and use MCP, but the pair lacks a documented shared channel or parser bridge. The only plausible pathway is manual copy-paste or shared files, which is unusual and limited.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies B-generated text into A's workflow
IF both agents are pointed at the same mounted file and A treats that file as instructions
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate workspaces
Disable MCP servers for B unless needed
Use a read-only handoff file for any text transfer
Add a human review step before copying B output into A

B_data_leakage.rationale: B explicitly reads files in its runtime and has broad network egress, so any sensitive content mounted into the shared workspace can be transmitted. A is a docs-style content-writing repo with no runtime isolation fields, so the pair offers no documented barrier preventing sensitive files from reaching B's outputs or network calls.
conditions: IF sensitive files are mounted into B's runtime
IF B is configured to send file contents to a model provider or external API
mitigations: Do not mount sensitive files into B
Use a redacted copy of the workspace
Restrict B network egress during review runs
Separate credentials from any shared runtime volume
requires-engineering: add workspace-level data classification filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no declared write or concurrency capabilities, while B can write the filesystem and modify git state. The pair therefore has overlapping mutable-resource risk only if A's content is also placed in B's writable runtime or repo checkout; uncertainty remains because A's execution surface is undocumented, so the safer medium choice is warranted.
conditions: IF A's files are mounted into the same writable directory that B edits
IF B is allowed to commit or rewrite git state in that directory
mitigations: Give B a separate clone or branch
Make A's source tree read-only to B
Require explicit lock/checkout before git writes
Limit B to a scratch directory for generated artifacts

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a prompt-engineering content repo, so its outputs may be treated as guidance; B is an agentic coding system that can execute shell, browser, and filesystem actions. If B consumes A's text as authoritative instructions without verification, mistakes can cascade into real actions. The interaction is inferred rather than directly documented, so medium is the conservative choice.
conditions: IF B is prompted to follow A's generated instructions without a verification step
IF B is allowed to execute shell or browser actions based on A's text
mitigations: Insert a verification checklist before execution
Require B to cite source lines before acting
Use a second reviewer for any action plan
Constrain B to dry-run mode for first pass

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or retention mismatch is documented for A, and B only states that it handles files mounted into the runtime plus model-provider API keys. Because the pairwise compliance surface is undocumented, only a low-risk gap is supportable; the other agent is cited because the risk arises from their combined handling of mounted files and external model calls.
conditions: IF regulated data is mounted into B's runtime
IF the configured model provider stores prompts or files outside the required residency boundary
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in the shared runtime
Use a provider with the required residency terms
Review retention settings for the configured model provider
Document the data class allowed in B's workspace
